features.headline: MLB free agency tracker: 2026-27 offseason trades, moves
features.desc: We've got you covered on all the major MLB hot stove signings and trades.
body: The 2026-27 MLB hot stove was lit just days after the Milwaukee Brewers hoisted the franchise's first World Series championship trophy.

All eyes this winter are on the free agency of two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. But he's not the only one who will make a splash in the market, with Freddya Peralta, Randy Arozarena, Seiya Suzuki and Michael King among the other free agents to watch.
Which teams will go big to contend for the 2027 World Series title? And who will make the trades and signings that have everyone buzzing?
Below is a running list of notable transactions and updates from throughout the MLB offseason.
First baseman Jake Bauers and the Boston Red Sox are in agreement on a four-year, $58 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
Reliever Evan Phillips and the Atlanta Braves are in agreement on a three-year, $35 million contract.
Jacob Young agreed to terms on a long-term contract with the Washington Nationals, president of baseball operations Paul Toboni announced.
Source: Detroit Tigers agree to one-year deal with reliever Emilio Pagan.
RHP Ryan Weiss agrees to $1.85M deal with San Diego Padres, sources say.
Mets re-sign pitcher Robert Stock to one-year contract.

New York Yankees closer David Bednar, Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki and Seattle Mariners outfielder Randy Arozarena were among eight players who received $23.15 million qualifying offers from their teams Monday.
Sources: Chicago Cubs decline $7.5 million option for pitcher Colin Rea.
San Diego Padres decline options on Nick Pivetta, Lucas Giolito, Griffin Canning; exercise option on Hart.

features.headline: Commanders QB Sam Hartman to star as 'The Bachelor' in milestone 30th season
features.desc: The 30th season of ABC's "The Bachelor" that will premiere in March 2027 will star the former Notre Dame standout.
body: After a two-year hiatus, "The Bachelor" has found the apple of its eye for its upcoming season: Sam Hartman.

On Friday, the hit reality dating show announced that the Washington Commanders backup quarterback will be the lead of its milestone 30th season. The premise of the show is Hartman finding love, with the goal of a marriage proposal by the finale.
But if the contestants want Hartman's heart, they might have to know ball a bit.

Hartman, 27, went undrafted in the 2024 NFL draft before the Commanders signed the former Notre Dame and Wake Forest standout to their practice squad after selecting Jayden Daniels with the No. 2 pick in that draft.
The Charlotte, North Carolina, native spent five seasons at Wake Forest (2018-22) and transferred to Notre Dame ahead of the 2023 season.
He averaged 8.2 yards per pass attempt, threw for 15,656 passing yards and 134 touchdowns, and completed 59.8% of his passes during his collegiate career.

Athletes being featured in "The Bachelor" franchise is nothing new, though. On the 29th season of the dating show, Grant Ellis — who played college basketball at Iona and Southern — held the titular role.
The show also counts a list of former NFL players as alumni, including Mel Owens, Jesse Palmer, Colton Underwood and Clay Harbor.
Jordan Rodgers, Josh Murray, Dale Moss and Matt James, who played for Wake Forest like Hartman, are other former college football players who have been featured in the franchise.
The season is slated to premiere in March on ABC.

features.headline: Joe Burrow is the MVP favorite, but is there a better betting value?
features.desc: Joe Burrow is the MVP favorite halfway through the season, but is he worth a bet, or are their better values?
body: Nine weeks into the 2026 NFL season, Joe Burrow has taken over the MVP odds board. I'm not ready to call this his award to lose, though.
Josh Allen and Brock Purdy both lead strong teams, Jordan Love is heating up, and Trevor Lawrence probably deserves more attention than he's getting.
The question is where we're getting paid enough to bet. Let's break down the favorites, their remaining schedules and whether there's a price worth grabbing before Sunday.
Here's a look at the top five players favored to win NFL MVP.
Odds by DraftKings. Odds for major NFL awards can be found here.
Burrow is — and should be — the favorite, as he has compiled 23 passing touchdowns (16 in his past four games) and completed 74% of his passes. What else do you want?
The schedule gives him room to keep going, too, with the Commanders, Saints and Browns up next after Sunday's game against the Steelers.
But I'm passing at +175. The Bengals are still fighting for their division at 6-2, while the Bills and 49ers are both 7-1.
The Steelers found something playing Cover 3 in their first meeting with the Bengals. That makes grabbing this line a bad bet during Burrow's hottest stretch at his shortest price.

With just 12 passing touchdowns, Allen might look further behind than he actually is. Add in his nine rushing scores and suddenly we're talking about 21 total scores for the quarterback of a one-loss team, one with wins over 6-2 Detroit and 6-2 Minnesota.

A matchup with the Jets this week gives Buffalo an opportunity to keep stacking wins and stat lines. Allen's rushing ability keeps him in the race, but Burrow has the stronger production, and Purdy's team has the same record at a bigger payout.

features.headline: 10 Best: Ranking the world's top men's soccer players ... again!
features.desc: Who is the best soccer player in the world at the November international break? ESPN's latest rankings are here.
body: For as much as I make fun of the Ballon d'Or process and how ridiculous the mushy, vague, contradictory criteria are, I think the voting journalists have probably gotten it right in each of the past three years. At least, they haven't gotten it wrong.

When I wrote up my theoretical ballots in each of the past three years, my three choices were Rodri, Ousmane Dembélé and Harry Kane — the three eventual winners. Once you move beyond the top pick, though, things start to get really weird.
Imagine watching the 2025-26 Premier League season and then finding out that Chelsea's Marc Cucurella got more Ballon d'Or votes than Arsenal's Gabriel Magalhães and William Saliba — combined.
Since the award tends to identify one of the best players on one of the best teams in the world, it does tend to identify a worthy winner. But it rarely identifies any other worthy winners.
Remember when Mohamed Salah led the Premier League in goals and assists two seasons ago for a dominant Liverpool team? He finished fourth, with a vote total closer to 30th than first.
Who, then, is the best player in the world right now? Or rather, who are the best players in the world right now?

In August, we launched the 10 Best List, a recurring look at who I'd estimate to be the — you got it — 10 best soccer players in the world. We're back, post-Harry Kane Ballon d'Or, to update the list.

As a reminder, I'm using this as my guidance: "If you added this player to an average round-of-16 Champions League team, how much more likely would the team be to win the tournament?" And if a player is injured or has been injured recently, I'm dropping him out of the top 10.

features.headline: NFC North: Bears win division? Cousins has Vikes in command?
features.desc: What will Kirk Cousins and Micah Parsons mean for the best division in football, or will the Bears hang on?
features.by: Courtney Cronin and Rob Demovsky and Kevin Seifert and Eric Woodyard
body: No one in the NFL was on a bigger high coming out of last weekend than the Green Bay Packers.
They trounced the defending AFC champion New England Patriots 45-27 and put together their best performance of the season to improve to 6-3.
And then Packers coach Matt LaFleur killed the buzz: "The reality is this: We're in last place in our division right now."
Such is life in the NFC North, the most victorious division in football, where the Chicago Bears are on top at 7-2, followed by the Detroit Lions (6-2), Minnesota Vikings (6-2) and Packers (6-3).

The NFC North is the seventh division since 2002 with all four teams above.500 through Week 9, according to ESPN Research. It has the best combined record (25-9, 73.5 winning percentage) by any division in the first nine weeks of a season under the current division format, which began 24 years ago.

The last time all four teams in a division had a winning record at this point in a season was 2023 with the AFC North. All four finished with winning records, and all but the Cincinnati Bengals (9-8) made the playoffs. The Baltimore Ravens made it to the AFC Championship Game.

On the flip side of that was the 2022 AFC East, which also had every team with a winning record through Week 9 but had only two teams reach the playoffs, and neither advanced past the divisional round.
ESPN's FPI gives the Bears the best shot at winning the division at 35.1%, ahead of the Vikings (29.7%), Lions (24.7%) and Packers (10.5%).
So what's real and what's not in the NFC North? Reporters Courtney Cronin (Bears), Rob Demovsky (Packers), Kevin Seifert (Vikings) and Eric Woodyard (Lions) give their insight:

features.headline: Don't be surprised if Jordan Love makes history and Mendoza performs like a QB1
features.desc: Elite WRs compensate for the lack of a running game in Green Bay, while there's unwarranted caution for Vegas' QB.
body: Each week in the NFL is its own story — full of surprises, both positive and negative — and fantasy football managers must decide what to believe and what not to believe moving forward. Perhaps we can help. If any of these thoughts come true... don't be surprised!
NOTE: All mention of fantasy points is for PPR formats, unless otherwise mentioned.
MVP candidate Love continues to shine, throwing for 372 yards in Sunday's high-scoring road victory over the New England Patriots.

With eight games left in the regular season, Love boasts a league-leading 2,618 passing yards, pacing toward 4,945 yards. Nine quarterbacks in NFL history have thrown for 5,000 yards, doing so 15 times.
Matthew Stafford, Justin Herbert, Patrick Mahomes (twice) and — of course — Jameis Winston are the only active QBs to have done so.

The Packers cannot run the football effectively, forcing Love to throw more than the team's original plan. Love threw for 4,159 yards in his first season as starter back in 2023 but had 11 interceptions, and the team went 9-8.

They wanted Love to take fewer chances, release the ball quicker and play more efficiently. Last season, the Packers went 9-5-1 in Love's 15 starts, as he threw for only 3,381 yards with a mere six interceptions.
The Packers were fifth in the league in rushing in 2024 and 15th in 2025. That plan worked, and it figured to be the plan again.
Let's just say things haven't worked out in the running game — thanks to offensive line and running back issues — and there is little indication that will change in the coming weeks and months.
